title: SPX Intraday IV Follows a U-Shape: Higher at Open and Close, Lower at Midday
claim: Implied volatility for at-the-money SPX options follows a predictable U-shaped intraday pattern — elevated in the first 30 minutes after open (9:30–10:00 ET) and the last 30 minutes before close (15:30–16:00 ET), and compressed during the midday period (11:30–13:30 ET). Selling ATM straddles at the open and buying them back at midday generates positive intraday premium capture on average across the trading day.
rationale: Market microstructure theory predicts that information asymmetry is highest at the open (overnight news resolution) and close (portfolio rebalancing flows), driving wider bid-ask spreads and elevated IV. The midday period is characterised by lower volume, lower directional pressure, and therefore lower realised vol — which should translate into IV compression. Sinclair's discussion of intraday realised vol patterns supports the observation that hourly realised vol is non-uniform across the trading day. If IV at the open consistently overestimates subsequent intraday realised vol by a measurable margin, selling the open and buying back at midday is a systematic edge.
testability_notes: Using SPX 1-minute OHLC data and ORATS intraday IV snapshots (if available) or reconstructed from bid-ask midpoints of ATM options 2015–2023: compute 30-minute realised vol buckets (9:30–10:00, 10:00–10:30 … 15:30–16:00). Separately compute ATM IV at each 30-minute interval. Measure IV-HV gap per time bucket. Falsified if the open/close IV-HV gap is not significantly larger than midday gap. Secondary test: backtest open-sell / midday-buy ATM straddle across 200+ trading days.
data_required: SPX 1-minute OHLC data 2015–2023; intraday ATM IV snapshots from ORATS or CBOE LiveVol
what_would_support: Open/close IV-HV gap > midday gap by > 1 vol point on average; open-sell/midday-buy straddle Sharpe > 0.3
what_would_reject: No significant intraday IV pattern, or midday IV higher than open IV on average
rejection_reason: Claim has no conditional language. Claim: implied volatility for at-the-money spx options follows a predictable u-shaped intraday pattern — el

title: Intraday VIX Futures Roll Yield Is Concentrated in the First and Last Hour
claim: The daily roll yield from holding short VIX front-month futures (contango decay) is not earned uniformly throughout the trading day. Approximately 60–70% of the daily contango decay accrues in the first 60 minutes (9:30–10:30 ET) and the final 30 minutes (15:30–16:00 ET), while the midday period contributes less than 30% of total daily roll. Strategies that are short VIX futures only during these two windows would capture most of the contango benefit with significantly lower intraday exposure.
rationale: The VIX term structure and contango theme in this knowledge base establishes that the roll yield is a structural feature driven by mean reversion of front-month IV to back-month levels. Intraday, this mean reversion is not uniform: institutional hedging demand is highest at open and close, causing IV to be temporarily elevated in these windows. The VIX front-month future's price relative to fair-value spot VIX should therefore be largest (most overpriced) at open and close, meaning the decay is concentrated there. If true, partial-day exposure strategies (open + close only) can extract most of the contango yield while avoiding the flat midday period where the carry is lower and bid-ask friction is proportionally larger.
testability_notes: Using VIX front-month futures 15-minute settlement data from CBOE 2010–2023: compute the returns from holding short VIX futures in each 30-minute intraday window (9:30–10:00, 10:00–10:30 … 15:30–16:00). Aggregate returns by window across contango periods only. Compare the sum of first-60-min and last-30-min returns to total daily return. Falsified if roll yield is distributed uniformly across windows (i.e., each 30-minute window contributes equally, at 1/13 of total). Test if open+close-only exposure achieves > 55% of full-day return with < 40% of full-day exposure time.
data_required: CBOE VIX front-month futures 15-minute or 30-minute intraday settlement data 2010–2023
what_would_support: Open 60-min + close 30-min periods contribute > 55% of total daily roll yield in contango regimes; statistically significant concentration
what_would_reject: Roll yield uniformly distributed across intraday windows; open+close-only exposure captures < 40% of full-day return
rejection_reason: Claim has no measurable variable. Claim: the daily roll yield from holding short vix front-month futures (contango decay) is not earned unifo

title: QQQ Daily Volume Predicts Same-Day Realized Volatility With Correlation > 0.60
claim: QQQ daily trading volume exhibits a Spearman correlation greater than 0.60 with same-day realized volatility (absolute close-to-close return), consistent with the volume-volatility relationship documented empirically for SPY.
rationale: Sinclair (Figure 3.8-3.9) reports SPY correlation between daily range and volume = 0.81, and absolute returns vs volume = 0.68. If this holds for QQQ (a correlated ETF), it implies volume is a real-time signal for volatility regime — tradeable for same-day position sizing or hedging adjustments.
testability_notes: Fetch QQQ daily volume and close prices from Databento, 2024-01-01 to 2026-04-01. Compute |return| = |ln(close_t/close_{t-1})|. Compute Spearman correlation between daily volume and |return|. Also compute rolling 20-day correlation. Support: overall Spearman r > 0.60 AND p < 0.001. Falsification: r < 0.40. Subgroup: r for days where volume > 1.5x median vs < 0.75x median.
what_would_support: Spearman r between daily volume and |return| > 0.60, p < 0.001
rejection_reason: Claim has no conditional language. Claim: qqq daily trading volume exhibits a spearman correlation greater than 0.60 with same-day realized vo
